PullRequest.Title: automations: fix: show feedback while dragging an automation file to import
PullRequest.Body:

## Why
Dragging an `.automation.md` file onto the Automations page gave no feedback, so it was unclear where to drop it. The page did have an overlay, but it never showed during a real drag. It decided visibility from `dataTransfer.files` and `getData`, which Chromium hides until `drop`. Unit tests passed only because a synthetic `DataTransfer` isn't protected.

## What changed
- A new [`AutomationImportDropTarget`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ulugbekna/agents/poteto-mode-solution-proposals/src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationImportDropTarget.ts) decides hover feedback only from what a drag exposes (transfer types, each item's kind and MIME type) and validates the file on drop. Its overlay covers only the part of the target on screen, so the label stays visible when the page or the modal is scrolled. The Automations page and the Automations modal both use it. The modal had no drop support before.
- **Accepted drag** (one text or untyped file, or an in-app file drag): the shared `editorGroup.dropBackground` tint and an "Import Automation File" label using the window's `.drop-overlay-label` style, like the chat and editor drop overlays.
- **Rejected drag** (several files, or a non-text file such as a PNG): no tint, an error label that says why, and a not-allowed cursor.
- **Wrong file name after drop** (e.g. `notes.md`; names are hidden while hovering): an error notification naming the file, with an **Import Automation...** action, instead of a modal dialog.
- The page fills the view body so the whole body accepts the drop, and its empty state says "or drop an .automation.md file here to import it".

## Tradeoffs
- A file with an empty MIME type is accepted on hover, because some platforms report no type for Markdown. Its name is checked on drop.
- The view header and side margins outside the content column don't accept drops. They belong to the shared custom view host.

## Verification
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationImportDropTarget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationsTable.test.ts`: 315 passing. New tests simulate Chromium's protected drag data, and cover a scrolled ancestor and a scrolled target; both fail on the old code.
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`, `pnpm run stylelint`, `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: clean.
- Running Code OSS Agents window, with real Chromium drags (`Input.dispatchDragEvent` with files, where names are hidden until drop): accepted, several files, PNG, `notes.md` drop, valid drop opening the prefilled review dialog, the modal, the high contrast theme, and a tall page scrolled 600px down (overlay matched the visible scroller, label centered on screen). The "copilot-chat failed" toast in the screenshots comes from the dev build not having the Copilot extension built.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: NotificationService.prompt wraps the choice in ChoiceAction, which retains and invokes choice.run; NotificationsModel retains the action until notification closure. Error notifications with actions are sticky. AutomationsEditor clears/disposes its widget on hide or clearInput, but drop-target disposal does not clear its readonly root reference. Notification equality compares messages, so distinct rejected filenames avoid deduplication. This is a static retention-chain finding; retained byte size is not measured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Disposed AutomationImportDropTarget instances and their detached root DOM subtrees, including remaining controls and automation detail text.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One retained root per disposed widget generation that still has at least one distinct outstanding invalid-drop notification, not one root per drop within the same widget. Identical messages deduplicate; distinct filenames do not. Memory scales with those retained generations and their remaining DOM/text size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary retained memory accumulates across disposed widget generations and cannot be reclaimed while their notifications remain open.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The page displayed an error dialog using message/detail strings without registering a callback that retained its owner after dismissal. The modal had no import-drop notifications.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Invalid drops now create sticky error notifications whose Import action strongly references the AutomationImportDropTarget instance, allowing the notification lifetime to outlast the owning widget and retain its root DOM.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added callback at automationImportDropTarget.ts:254 captures `this` in a notification action. The previous page rejection path called dialogService.error with strings and installed no persistent callback referring to the drop target; the modal previously had no drop handler.
Findings.Title: Avoid retaining the drop target in the notification action
Findings.Impact: Drop a wrongly named file, then close or switch away from the Automations modal without dismissing the notification. The disposed drop target and detached modal DOM remain in memory. Repeating this across widget recreations with different rejected filenames retains additional roots until the notifications are dismissed.
Findings.Evidence: notificationService.ts:258-323 stores choices in actions and disposes them only on handle.onDidClose; notifications.ts:226-239 retains notifications in the model, :636-645 makes errors with actions sticky, and :815-820 retains choice.run. The new drop target stores root at :155 and only removes the overlay/class at :174-177. automationsEditor.ts:89-103 clears the modal widget on hide/clearInput, while automationsModalWidget.ts:114 removes its DOM root without clearing its contents. Raw detail text, including automation prompts (:493-503), therefore remains reachable through the disposed root.
Findings.Recommendation: Capture the command service in a local variable and have the notification action use that variable, rather than capturing the drop-target instance. This preserves the action after widget disposal without retaining the DOM owner.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, resize, and dispose the Automations page or modal without importing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing widget construction and initial rendering must finish before interaction. The diff adds one hidden overlay and label per widget and registers disposable drag listeners. Page catalogue refresh remains asynchronous rather than blocking construction; the existing refresh timer remains unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing asynchronous refresh of the automation provider stores and their catalogues/history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical refresh per registered automation store per page refresh, not per automation card; the existing page timer repeats after 60 seconds. Provider-specific downstream grouping and limits are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The page already refreshed those stores on construction and on the same timer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial widget-construction critical path; data arrival updates existing renderers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing automation, template, and history collections control renderer size. New drop-target allocation is constant per widget, not per row or card.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing provider refresh uses Promise.all over stores. DOM construction/layout remains synchronous. Drag observer and overlay teardown are owned by the widget's disposable store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing provider catalogue/history state is reused. AutomationDialogService is registered as delayed and has an empty constructor; creating the drop target does not open the heavyweight import dialog. No new caches or retained collection keys are added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in constant-size construction and unchanged refresh scheduling, from constructors, service registration, and resize/scroll host code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime layout or startup profile was available. The extra hidden DOM and CSS layout changes are bounded; no resize feedback loop was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent startup, fan-out, or normal-disposal regression. Disposal after an outstanding invalid-drop notification is covered separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover accepted, rejected, or unrelated drags over the page or modal, including a scrolled target or ancestor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each dragenter/dragover callback synchronously classifies exposed transfer items and positions feedback before returning to the browser. Ignored drags skip geometry work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read browser geometry/computed styles for the root and clipping ancestors, then write the overlay's absolute bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root measurement and one computed-style lookup per ancestor per applicable drag event, with extra geometry reads only for clipping ancestors. Cost scales with ancestor depth, not automation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old page overlay used CSS inset bounds and no geometry walk; the modal had no import overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on the UI event path; required to keep the overlay within the visible scrolled region.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Transfer-item count F and DOM ancestor depth D determine O(F + D) hover work. One target handles the event; there is no per-card drop target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DragAndDropObserver invokes callbacks directly on the UI thread without throttling. Geometry reads are grouped before the main overlay writes; there is no IPC, filesystem, subprocess, database, or network work during hover.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Feedback equality suppresses repeated class/label reconstruction and live-region updates. Geometry is deliberately recalculated to follow scrolling. Hover no longer extracts protected editor payloads or reads file contents.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the new bounded synchronous geometry walk and render deduplication; insufficient evidence of a concrete user-visible latency regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No browser trace establishes materially expensive forced layouts or dropped frames. Ancestor depth is bounded by the UI hierarchy, and positioning during scrolling is intentional.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence reportable hover-performance regression; do not infer jank from geometry API names alone.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop one valid automation blueprint and review/save it on the existing Automations page.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validate the deduplicated drop resources, read and decode one file, and parse its blueprint before showing the review dialog. Saving then waits for existing draft/customization synchronization and persistence to the explicitly selected provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse editor/resource transfer payloads and deduplicate resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction per drop; duplicate representations of the same URI are coalesced before the single-file check. Multiple distinct resources are rejected without content reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The page used the same extraction on drop and additionally attempted extraction during hover.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one validated resource through IFileService, or read a browser File through arrayBuffer, and decode its bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical file-content read per valid drop, zero for rejected drops; bytes scale with that file's size B.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old page handleDrop used the identical resource-read/arrayBuffer and VSBuffer decoding paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Read and decode finish before parseAutomationBlueprint and the review dialog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For an Agent Host destination, capture existing customization inputs and dispatch AutomationCreateRequested, then wait for authoritative catalogue state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create dispatch to the explicitly selected provider per confirmed import, not one per provider or catalogue entry. Customization work remains in the unchanged provider implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same importAutomationBlueprint commit callback already routed to this provider operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the confirmed-save critical path, not on hover or before file validation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For a cloud destination, resolve the selected repository, read its automation configuration, and send the create request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected repository, one configuration request and one create request per confirmed import, plus unchanged account/repository resolution if needed; not a request per automation or workspace candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing page import and Import Automation command used this same provider path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration precedes creation; both are awaited before save completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Transfer resources after URI deduplication must have cardinality one. File read/decode/parse scales with B. Provider creation routes to one destination regardless of catalogue size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No bulk import or new parallel fan-out. Existing dialog save guards prevent overlapping saves within a dialog. Cloud mutations use a per-store Sequencer; Agent Host create dispatch waits for authoritative state. Existing draft synchronization uses generation/cancellation checks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No content cache was added or removed; both cold and repeated imports read the selected file once. Existing draft synchronization reuses a matching target and customization loading is keyed by target; cloud mutations still perform their authoritative configuration check even with cached catalogue entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged page file I/O, decoding, dialog invocation, and selected-provider routing from the old/new drop handlers and importAutomationBlueprint.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-file parse/read costs and provider latency are not measured, but their placement and cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No page import-throughput, allocation, or boundary-count regression. Large-file and provider costs predate this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop one valid automation blueprint directly onto the modal, which now supports import.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new drop entry point validates one file and invokes the same read/parse/review/save sequence as the page and existing Import Automation command. No import work starts merely by opening the modal or hovering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/decode the single dropped file before opening the prefilled review dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical content read per explicitly valid drop; zero reads for invalid or unrelated drops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The modal had no direct drop import. Users could invoke the existing Import Automation command, which read one chosen file and opened the same review flow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist a confirmed import to the selected Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create dispatch for the selected provider only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Not reachable through a modal drop, but already reachable through the existing import command with the same dispatch count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only after the user confirms save.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist a confirmed import to the selected cloud repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration check and one create request for one repository, with unchanged optional resolution/authentication work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Not reachable through a modal drop; the existing import command reached the identical cloud workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only after confirmed save; cloud operations remain sequenced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one validated file after resource deduplication; its byte size controls reading/parsing. One selected destination controls persistence, not all available providers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new handler launches one shared import flow per user drop. Existing dialog save guards and provider scheduling remain unchanged; no loop launches imports for all dropped files.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the existing dialog/service caches and target deduplication. No new cache, negative-cache behavior, or repeated background file reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in one-file validation and reuse of the unchanged import helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Import duration depends on file size and provider availability. Added costs are explicit requested feature work, not unnecessary eager or repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: New user-requested capability without an independently established performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reject an invalid drop, leave its notification open, dispose/recreate the widget, or choose the recovery Import action.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Invalid drops only extract/validate metadata and create an error notification; they do not read file contents. The recovery file picker/import runs only after an explicit action click. Notifications remain owned by the global notification model after widget disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain a sticky notification action whose closure captures the drop target and therefore its root DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retained root for each disposed widget generation with at least one outstanding distinct invalid-drop message. Multiple drops within the same widget share its root, and identical messages deduplicate. Distinct rejected filenames preserve separate messages and can retain different generations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The page reported rejection through a dialog using strings, without an owner-capturing recovery action. The modal had no import-drop notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Retention is off the immediate import critical path but prevents reclamation across navigation/close cycles until notification dismissal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the existing file picker from the notification's recovery action; desktop-native picker handling is platform-dependent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One picker invocation per explicit action click, with canSelectMany=false; selected-file reading and provider persistence then have the same single-file cardinality as above.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same picker was already reachable through the Import Automation command, but not this notification action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks the user-requested recovery import, not rejection feedback or widget construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct outstanding rejected filenames combined with widget recreation, not total files dragged or automation count alone. Each retained root contributes its remaining detached DOM and text, including modal detail prompts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Notification creation and model retention are synchronous. Persistence of old notifications is independent of widget teardown. Recovery executes one existing import command per click.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Notification equality uses message and action identity/label, so identical rejections replace an older notification while differing filenames do not. These errors have actions and are sticky. Drop-target disposal removes listeners/overlay but leaves the readonly root reference reachable through the action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: ChoiceAction retains choice.run; the new callback captures this; the global model retains sticky notifications until close; modal hide/clearInput disposes the widget without severing the drop target's root reference.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No heap profile measures retained bytes or how often users keep different rejection notifications open across navigation. This lowers severity, not confidence in the explicit retention chain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one low-severity cleanup-lifecycle memory regression at automationImportDropTarget.ts:254. Capture the command service instead of the DOM-owning drop target.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all nine changed files and every diff page against base 384f593b5a4c1315b1168e4d4b32e9168752f6a0. Traced drag-event geometry, render deduplication, widget disposal, notification ownership/deduplication, single-file reads and parsing, delayed dialog construction, and selected-provider IPC/network persistence. Submitted one high-confidence low-severity notification-lifetime DOM-retention finding. No concrete historical performance fix qualified for blame-based learning. Static read-only review; no measured layout, timing, or heap results.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
